_comment: Advisories accepted as residual risk, enforced by scripts/audit-ci.mjs. Every entry lists the installed version, the full dependency path, whether an upstream fix exists, the exposure classification, and a review_by date. Once review_by passes, the audit gate fails until the entry is re-justified or removed. None of these advisories are reachable on the deployed static site or in a visitor's browser.

advisories.reason: image-size <= 2.0.2 has infinite-loop DoS bugs in its ICNS (GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr) and JXL/HEIF (GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq) decoders. image-size runs only during `docusaurus build`, when Docusaurus reads the intrinsic dimensions of images referenced from Markdown/MDX. It is never bundled into the deployed site and never runs in a browser. Exploitation requires committing a crafted ICNS/JXL/HEIF file to this repo's own content. image-size 2.0.3+ fixes it, but @docusaurus/mdx-loader (through 3.10.2) has an exact pin on image-size@2.0.2, so there is no lockfile-only or overrides-based fix that stays on the Docusaurus dependency set.
advisories.upstream: https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus — needs a Docusaurus release that bumps @docusaurus/mdx-loader's image-size pin

advisories.reason: serialize-javascript before 7.0.5 can be driven to RCE via RegExp.flags / Date.prototype.toISOString (GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq, high) or to CPU exhaustion via crafted array-like objects (GHSA-qj8w-gfj5-8c6v, moderate) when it serializes attacker-controlled objects. In this chain it is only ever handed this repo's own webpack build configuration by copy-webpack-plugin / css-minimizer-webpack-plugin during `docusaurus build`. No user or content input reaches it and nothing from it ships to the deployed site. Both webpack plugins are transitive deps of @docusaurus/bundler with no local override that keeps the bundler working; npm audit reports fixAvailable:false.
advisories.upstream: https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus — needs @docusaurus/bundler to bump copy-webpack-plugin / css-minimizer-webpack-plugin

advisories.fix_available: npm reports fixAvailable:true, but the only fix is uuid@11 — a major bump of sockjs's declared uuid@^8.3.2 dependency, not a semver-safe lockfile-only update
advisories.reason: uuid before 11.1.1 (GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq) is missing a buffer-bounds check in the v3/v5/v6 generators, but only on the code path where the caller passes a `buf` argument. sockjs calls `uuid.v4()` with no arguments, so the vulnerable branch is never entered. The dependency also exists only under webpack-dev-server, i.e. during `npm start` on a developer's localhost — it is not part of `docusaurus build` output and never runs on the deployed site. sockjs 0.3.24 (latest) still declares uuid@^8.3.2; forcing uuid@11 via `overrides` is a cross-major jump on a transitive-of-a-transitive and is deliberately not done here.
advisories.upstream: https://github.com/sockjs/sockjs-node — needs sockjs to widen / bump its uuid dependency

advisories.exposure: dev-only test runner / vulnerable code path not installed
advisories.path: devDependencies > vitest@2.1.9 (only used by `npm test` == `vitest run`)
advisories.fix_available: npm reports fixAvailable: vitest@4.1.11 (isSemVerMajor: true) — a 2.x -> 4.x major bump. No patched 2.1.x or 3.x exists; the advisory range is <=3.2.5.
advisories.reason: GHSA-5xrq-8626-4rwp requires the Vitest UI server to be listening (`vitest --ui`, which loads @vitest/ui) for an attacker page to read/execute arbitrary files. This repo does NOT install @vitest/ui and never passes --ui: the only invocation is the headless `vitest run` in `npm test` on a developer's machine / CI. npm audit flags the `vitest` metapackage by version range regardless of whether the UI package is present, so the vulnerable code is not on disk here. vitest and its whole tree are devDependencies and are excluded from the published package (the `files` whitelist ships only index.js, tokens/, lib/, src/components|data|utils, src/infima-bridge.css, assets/) — nothing reaches @zcohen-nerd/brand consumers or the deployed sites. The upstream fix is vitest 4, which also drops the direct `esbuild` import this repo's vitest.config.mjs uses for the JSX-in-.js transform; migrating that config + re-verifying the 26 component tests is a scheduled maintenance task, not a release-blocker.
advisories.upstream: https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest — fixed in vitest 4.x; local action is a config migration off the esbuild JSX transform, tracked for the next maintenance window

advisories.fix_available: Only via vitest@4.1.11 (isSemVerMajor: true) — see the vitest entry. `npm audit fix` applied every semver-safe update; the remaining vite advisories are pinned by vitest 2.x's dependency range.
advisories.reason: The vite advisories (path traversal in optimized-deps `.map` handling; `server.fs.deny` bypass on Windows alternate paths; launch-editor NTLM hash disclosure) are all against the Vite dev server / file-serving layer. Vite is present here only as a transitive dependency of vitest 2.1.9 and is exercised solely by the headless `vitest run` test process on a developer's machine / CI — no Vite dev server is started, and nothing from this tree is bundled into @zcohen-nerd/brand or any deployed site (devDependencies, excluded from the `files` whitelist). Clears together with the vitest 4 upgrade.
advisories.upstream: https://github.com/vitejs/vite — pulled in by vitest; resolved by the vitest 4 upgrade
